card.name: Writing verbs and letter after an author
card.fires_on: The words wrote, written, letter or essay right after a named author or a possessive such as 'Paul's' or 'his'. It marks a writer's piece of writing about to be quoted or described.

modes.label: Wrote / written
modes.description: A past-tense writing verb follows a named person, introducing what they said.
modes.example: "A sad soul can kill you quicker, far quicker, than a germ," John Steinbeck once<< wrote>>. Now we are closer to understanding why

modes.label: Letter or essay
modes.description: The noun letter or essay follows a writer's name, a possessive or 'a'.
modes.example: In the spring of 1862 she wrote a<< letter>> to Higginson beginning, Are

card.plain: It fires on words like wrote or letter when someone is quoted or cited as the author of a text.
